verdicts.evidence: On /barn/editor the stream ([data-testid=barn-activity-stream]) held 50 entries built from the pod's own record (/app/.barn/provenance.jsonl, 25 turns). Sent "w4-workspace probe 1787513612045" from the composer: a user turn appeared in the stream at once, and 20s later it was the pod's copy that was showing - the caption read "Sent from the workspace screen by Default Admin", which only the pod's record carries, and the matching line is in provenance.jsonl with screen "workspace" and who "Default Admin". The stream was scrolled to the bottom (scrollHeight - scrollTop - clientHeight = under 60px) with the newest turn visible.

Clicked into the field, typed "line one", Shift+Enter, "line two": the value became two lines and nothing was sent. The placeholder is 'Describe the next change - e.g. "colour the bars by severity and add a 7-day toggle"' and it is gone as soon as there is text. Sending the draft put it in the stream and in the pod's provenance log.

Both halves of the line are true now. The workspace does autosave: with the editor open I wrote W4-AUTOSAVE-1787516372511 into a file in the pod, and 10 seconds later a new tag barn-snap/1787516405029 "autosave 2020 on Aug 23" existed, whose tree really holds my edit (git show barn-snap/1787516405029:verify-w4-workspace.txt returns exactly that marker). Nobody took it by hand. It is rate limited from the newest snapshot in the pod rather than per tab: the gaps between consecutive autosave tags over an hour were 188, 181, 182, 181, 180, 184, 184 and 180 seconds - never under three minutes - while the two safety snapshots taken by an apply and a roll back sat between them at 47s and 62s, as they should. A second edit ten seconds after an autosave produced no new snapshot for at least 110 seconds; the readout just kept counting up. And the readout is a real clock on the newest snapshot: "Snapshot saved 27h ago" on arrival with one 27-hour-old tag in the pod, then "Snapshot saved 9s / 2m / 3m ago" as they were taken, with the tooltip naming the snapshot it is reporting. Finally, it says so when it fails: with .git/objects and .git/refs root-owned in the pod and the tree moving, the line changed to "Autosave failed - last snapshot 4m ago" and the tooltip to "The tree has changed and it could not be snapshotted, so nothing since \"autosave 2020 on Aug 23\" is kept: the snapshot of base failed in the pod (exit 1): error: insufficient permission for adding an object to repository ...". Ownership put back afterwards and normal autosaving resumed.
verdicts.defect: One gap, in a state that is worse than the one it handles: if git cannot be read at all (the whole .git root-owned, which is what "chown -R root:root .git" gives you), workingDiff() comes back empty through inPackage's non-strict path instead of throwing, so autoSnapshot never gets as far as createSnapshot, autoError is never set, and the line reads "No snapshot yet" with the tooltip still promising "the tree is watched and one is taken automatically when it changes". Nothing is being watched and nothing can be written. The narrower failure (refs/objects unwritable) is reported correctly, which is the case the message was written for.

verdicts.defect: The band names the files but not the baseline: it says "differ from the baseline" instead of "differ from the last commit". baselineRef() in extensions.ts always fails - the script it sends is joined into "... ; for r in A B ; do ; git rev-parse ..." and the "do ;" is a shell syntax error, so the pod answers nothing, the kind falls back to 'none' and BASELINE_NOUNS['none'] is ''. Verified by running the composed script in the pod: "/bin/sh: 1: Syntax error: ";" unexpected", exit 2. The same call feeds BuildFailure.findWayBack, where it silently removes the "last version published" rung of the roll-back ladder. Noted while writing this up: the working tree already carries a fix (join with a newline instead of ' ; '), but it is not in the installed bundle this wave was judged against.

verdicts.defect: devServerLog() in extensions.ts fetches the pod-log subresource with { headers: { Accept: 'text/plain' } }. The Kubernetes apiserver rejects that: 406 NotAcceptable, "only the following media types are accepted: application/json, application/yaml, application/vnd.kubernetes.protobuf". Verified from the page: the same URL with no Accept header, or with Accept: */*, returns 200 text/plain with the log. Dropping the header fixes it. Until then the strip expands onto an error every time. Noted while writing this up: the working tree already carries that fix, but it is not in the installed bundle this wave was judged against.

Drove both outcomes against a file of my own. Refusal first: with .git/objects and .git/refs root-owned in the pod, clicking "Roll back to ..." gave "The roll back did not happen - Nothing has been rolled back. The failed tree could not be snapshotted first, and this panel will not replace a tree it cannot put back: the snapshot of base failed in the pod (exit 1): error: insufficient permission for adding an object to repository database .git/objects ...". Afterwards the file was byte-for-byte unchanged, the snapshot count was still 18, the failure card was still on screen, the badge still read Failed and the button was still offered. Then chowned back to 1000:1000, wrote refs/barn/working-build at a commit holding the tree, and the button relabelled itself "Roll back to the last working build (9.9.9-w4)". Changed my file to W4-ROLLBACK-MODIFIED and clicked: toast "Rolled back to the last working build (9.9.9-w4) - The failed tree was snapshotted first, so nothing is lost.", the file was back to W4-ROLLBACK-BEFORE, a new tag "the failed build before rolling back" existed and git show of my file at that tag returned W4-ROLLBACK-MODIFIED, the failure card was gone and the badge went back to Unsaved. The ref was removed afterwards.

The workspace masthead's controls are back, the name, the state badge, the branch menu, "Preview on: local", the phase chip, the publish status slot, the snapshots clock, Undo, "Review N changes", the extension picker, Publish, settings and the overflow. The snapshots menu's "Restore the tree to <snapshot>" is a different action: it does not resolve the last working build.
